kind: A diagnostic in floats on the Transformer reference, by slope over data, on the server's CPU, two seeds. Its arms are Transformers with other units: they are no spiking networks, never a path for this project and never a result of it. They say which gate a spiking cell needs. Recorded before any run of it started.
why: The first seed of plain_units_with_data says that a unit which multiplies keeps learning where a plain one falls behind. Against the gated reference (swiglu) on the test bed's Transformer, plain rectifying units go from 0.032 ahead after 6,000 updates to 0.011 behind after 24,000 and plain smooth units from 0.024 ahead to 0.003 behind, while a gated unit that is shut below zero and opens in proportion above it (reglu) goes from 0.007 ahead to 0.001 ahead. The stack's cells are plain, and its gap to the Transformer grows with data. So the cell that multiplies stays the target, if the second seed agrees. But the gate that kept pace is not bounded: at twice the drive it passes its value twice. Every gated cell that the stack has trained with data had a bounded gate. A shunt lets in k / (k + 4) of the value for k gate spikes and never all of it: 0.118 behind at full size, 0.113 behind under the pool that lifts the ceiling (full_size_unit_screen.json, full_size_lifted_gate.json). A gate that opens in proportion lets in all of the value at 16 thresholds and no more: 0.65 and 0.80 behind after 24,000 updates on two seeds, once it had turned into a switch (proportional_gates_with_data.json). They were bounded on purpose, because the stack's first multiplying gate let in up to sixteen times the value and left the range in which a cell learns. If a bound on the gate loses the gated unit's lead in floats too, those cells failed for what they compute, and the next spiking gate has to multiply without a bound. If bounded gates keep the lead in floats, they failed for how a gate learns through spikes, and the work belongs there. Shazeer's comparison of feed-forward units in a Transformer (GLU Variants Improve Transformer, 2020, table 1) points at the first: after 65,536 steps the logistic gate was level with plain smooth units (1.982 against 1.983, plain rectifying units 1.997), where the gates that are linear in their drive scored 1.953 (rectified) and 1.944 (smooth) and the plain product of two drives 1.960; after 524,288 steps the logistic gate had a third of the lead (1.663 against 1.677 for plain rectifying units, 1.645 for the rectified gate, 1.636 for the smooth one and 1.648 for the product). That is another task, size and length than the test bed's.

arms.rampglu: --feed-forward rampglu: the gate opens in proportion to its drive and is wide open at a drive of one, min(max(g, 0), 1) times the value. The float form of the stack's proportional gate (--granule-ramp).
arms.shuntglu: --feed-forward shuntglu: the gate is a conductance, g / (1 + g) of the value above zero and nothing below. The float form of the stack's shunting gate (--granule-shunt), the gate of both full-size gated arms.
arms.sigglu: --feed-forward sigglu: the logistic gate, between nothing and all of the value and half open at a drive of zero. A bounded gate that opens smoothly and rests half open, the float form of a gate with a set point, which the roadmap lists as untried.
arms.bilinear: --feed-forward bilinear: no gate, the product of the two drives, of either sign. It asks whether the unit needs its gate shut on one side, or only the product.

base: The arms of plain_units_with_data at the same seed, length, rate and device: swiglu (the reference's own unit; seed 20001: 1.666476 after 6,000 updates and 1.446081 after 24,000) is the base of every pair, and reglu (1.659656 and 1.445502) is the gate without a bound that each bounded gate is read beside.
parameters: 4,792,320 for every arm, as the gated reference: a control gate has the gated unit's weights
training: As plain_units_with_data: the test bed's Transformer (--variant transformer --dim 256 --depth 6 --heads 4 --mlp-ratio 4; windows of 256 bytes in batches of 16; warmup 300 and a cosine over the run; weight decay 0.05; rotated Adam 50; averaged weights 0.999; the training mixture) at a peak rate of 1.2e-3, as separate runs of 6,000 and 24,000 updates, seed 20001 and then seed 20002, on the server's CPU with 8 threads a run and three runs side by side, after that study's remaining runs. Code: 175cf0a, in which the reference's own units compute what they did.
measure: As plain_units_with_data: experiments/eval_taught_reference.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes, in windows that hold 240 bytes of history and score 16, averaged weights, bits kept, on the CPU. Pairs by experiments/compare_stream_scores.py, and experiments/gap_by_piece.py (near 240, far 8,192) for the bytes in new contexts. On the first 65,536 validation bytes of every arm at both lengths: experiments/unit_density.py (the share of units whose gate's drive is above zero, and the share that passes nine tenths of a block's output), and for the three bounded gates how far an open gate stands open: the share of open gate states that let in more than three quarters of the value, the measure by which the stack's gates were found to work as switches.
reading: An arm's gap is its bits minus swiglu's at the same length and seed, and its growth is its gap at 24,000 updates less its gap at 6,000, read over the mean of both seeds with the marks of plain_units_with_data: growth from 0.015 on, none below 0.005, unclear between. On the first seed plain rectifying units grew by 0.043, plain smooth units by 0.027 and reglu by 0.006. (A) If all three bounded gates grow and reglu does not, a bound on the gate loses the gated unit's lead with data in floats as in the stack: the stack's gated cells failed for what they compute, the next spiking gate multiplies without a bound (the multiplying gate under the pool that lifts the ceiling, with no shunt and no ramp), and a shunt, a ramp or a set point is not tried again. (B) If no bounded gate grows, a bound costs nothing in floats: the stack's gated cells failed for how a gate learns through spikes, bounded gates stay candidates, and the work goes to the gate's learning (what turns a graded gate into a switch, the range rule, a decay or a set point on the gate's drive). (C) If the bounded gates differ, each is read by itself, and a gate that does not grow names the spiking form to try: the logistic gate a gate with a set point at half open, the shunt or the ramp the stack's own forms with another way to learn. The product is read by itself: if it does not grow, a cell may multiply two drives of either sign and needs no side on which its gate is shut; if it grows, the gate must be shut on one side. How far the open gates of a bounded arm stand open says whether a gate turns into a switch in floats as it does in spikes; it is reported and decides nothing. Reported beside all of it: each arm's gap at both lengths on new contexts, and the census.
seen_before_recording: The first seed of plain_units_with_data, complete: after 6,000 updates relu 1.634478, gelu 1.642148, reglu 1.659656, swiglu 1.666476; after 24,000 updates relu 1.457303, gelu 1.449175, reglu 1.445502, swiglu 1.446081, and relu at 2.4e-3 1.452757; of the second seed relu after 6,000 updates, 1.636921. The stack's gated-cell verdicts and the table of the paper named above. Dry runs of 60 updates with a warmup of 10 on a laptop CPU (validation on 8 batches of windows: swiglu 4.2052, reglu 4.2061, rampglu 4.2001, shuntglu 4.2430, sigglu 4.3283, bilinear 4.1654). A check of the stack's own multiplying gate under the lifting pool had started on the laptop and had shown nothing yet. No run of this study has started.
